newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatists warn of possible new attacks.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatists warn of possible new attacks.

text.p: Corsican separatists have warned Prime Minister Alain Juppe against any attempt to "physically eliminate" its members, saying its response would be extremely violent.

In a statement sent to state-owned regional television channel France-3 Corse on Thursday evening, the hardline Corsican National Liberation Front "Historic Wing" referred to investigations launched into a clandestine news conference held by nationalists in the Corsican hills on January 11.

Paris anti-terrorism magistrates had earlier on Thursday opened a probe into the news conference, at which the FLNC "Historic Wing" announced a three-month truce after a wave of bombings. The conference was attended by 600 hooded and armed men.

"Following the threats of arrests concerning the press conference, we declare to the envoy of the Elysee (presidential palace) and the prime minister that our organisation is ready to... explain the conditions under which this conference took place and the response that followed it," the statement said.
The government was reported to have used envoys to conduct secret talks with separatists which failed to reach a peace settlement.
The statement also cautioned that if the government tried to "physically eliminate" nationalists, then the FLNC would give a response of "incalculable violence".
Juppe has decreed a crackdown on violence in the French Mediterranean island but there have been few arrests so far.
Separatists took their battle for autonomy to the mainland in recent weeks, bombing the lawcourts in Aix-en-Provence and Juppe's mayoral offices in Bordeaux among other targets.
